builds.name: Reference: AP sustained duel
builds.goal: Reference for Mordekaiser: establish a repeatable reference
builds.hypothesis: A sustained melee magic fighter who activates an aura through contact and isolates a target for an extended duel. Keep passive activation, isolated Q and R duel state explicit. Shield-to-heal choices use the same stored resource; Dusk/on-hit value needs real attacks. AP plus real attack cadence tests sustained contact and later penetration.
builds.summary: AP plus real attack cadence tests sustained contact and later penetration.
testPlan: Kit question for Mordekaiser: Keep passive activation, isolated Q and R duel state explicit. Shield-to-heal choices use the same stored resource; Dusk/on-hit value needs real attacks.

Start with the early core (Riftmaker, then Nashor) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Use this as the control for the other three routes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Resource: Shield. Do not treat mana regeneration as Shield recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: AP plus real attack cadence tests sustained contact and later penetration. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern.

Q evidence: Mordekaiser smashes the ground with his mace dealing damage to each enemy struck. Damage is increased when hitting a single enemy. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Nashor needs actual attacks; little health/resistance makes CC and burst dangerous.

The route fails Mordekaiser's stated kit question: Keep passive activation, isolated Q and R duel state explicit. Shield-to-heal choices use the same stored resource; Dusk/on-hit value needs real attacks.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Nashor needs actual attacks; little health/resistance makes CC and burst dangerous.
Full cost 17,000 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
The reference is a research control, not a claim of the current highest-win-rate build.
buyOrder: Riftmaker, then Nashor. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Rabadon's Deathcap, Void Staff, Zhonya's Hourglass are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Resource: Shield. Do not treat mana regeneration as Shield recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Nashor realm execution
builds.summary: Spend the seven-second isolated duel on repeated AP attacks.
builds.goal: Spend the seven-second isolated duel on repeated AP attacks.
builds.hypothesis: Darkness Rise adds 0.4 AP magic damage to attacks and activates its aura after three qualifying attacks/basic abilities. Nashor and Dusk and Dawn add attack payloads, Terminus needs real attacks for mixed penetration and Riftmaker rewards the sustained Realm of Death. Q's isolation multiplier gives a spell payoff while R restricts the duel to one opponent.
testPlan: Required state: Need target access inside R, sufficient attack time and W shield management.
Compare attacks, passive activation and Q damage in seven-second duels versus a target with an escape.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: A slippery opponent can waste most of the seven seconds; low defenses make the exit dangerous.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Death Realm isolation does not remove enemy mobility or automatically fully stack Terminus.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Nashor's Tooth, Dusk and Dawn, Riftmaker, Terminus, Rabadon's Deathcap, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Bloodmail magic mace hybrid
builds.summary: Test Q's documented AD scaling without treating its damage as physical.
builds.goal: Test Q's documented AD scaling without treating its damage as physical.
builds.hypothesis: Obliterate has a 1.2 AD statFormula=2 term plus 0.7 AP and deals magic damage, amplified on a single target. Bloodmail's health-to-AD and Riftmaker's health-to-AP create a dual health conversion; Shojin increases qualifying spell/passive damage and Abyssal improves close magic output. Visage supports W's shield and optional remaining-shield healing.
testPlan: Required state: Need isolated Q hits, stored W damage and enough contact to ramp sustained effects.
Compare Q damage per gold and W absorption across bought-health levels, tracking physical attacks separately.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: AD does little for E/passive AP ratios; missing Q undermines the conversion payoff.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Lethality does not improve an AD-scaled magic Obliterate, and W recast spends the remaining shield.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Overlord's Bloodmail, Spear of Shojin, Riftmaker, Spirit Visage, Abyssal Mask, Mercury's Treads. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
